understand.title: Understand the Request
understand.instruction: Analyze the development request before proposing an implementation, using the Clear-Thought tools: run at least one sequential_thinking pass to structure the analysis and reference its conclusions in the submission. Provide a concise summary, assumptions, open questions, constraints, risks, measurable acceptance criteria, and affected areas. Do not create an implementation plan yet. Ask open questions in the chat before submitting and reference them in `openQuestions`; escalate via `report_blocker` ONLY when the answer would materially change this submission (a different plan or different code) — otherwise document the question, state your working assumption explicitly, and proceed. Submission idempotency: never reuse a requestId across submissions — each phase advance requires a fresh requestId; if a submission returns accepted but the phase is unchanged, do not retry the same requestId — check get_workflow_state (requestIds) instead. Clear-Thought MCP endpoint: http://host.docker.internal:3000/mcp. Timeout policy (FR-035, amended 2026-09-28): on a downstream MCP transport/request timeout retry ONCE — but only for read-only/idempotent calls; then use the tool's container route when available (the HTTP endpoint reachable from the guidance container, configured per server as containerRoute in downstream-servers.json; agent-side: run_operation through the guidance server) before falling back to local tools; route heavy GitNexus work (analyze/reindex) through the terminal CLI instead of MCP; after a second timeout, or for non-idempotent (workspace_write) calls, escalate via report_blocker (category: infrastructure) instead of retrying.
requiredActions: Run at least one Clear-Thought sequential_thinking pass and reference its conclusions in the submission.

plan.title: Create the Implementation Plan
plan.instruction: Target repository: zed. Create a concrete implementation plan with stable task identifiers, affected files, dependencies, planned tests, and verification, using the Clear-Thought tools: decompose and prioritize via sequential_thinking (and decision_framework when weighing alternatives), and reference the reasoning results in the submission. Do not start implementation yet. Submission idempotency: never reuse a requestId across submissions — each phase advance requires a fresh requestId; if a submission returns accepted but the phase is unchanged, do not retry the same requestId — check get_workflow_state (requestIds) instead. Ask open questions in the chat before submitting and reference them in `openQuestions`; escalate via `report_blocker` ONLY when the answer would materially change this submission (a different plan or different code) — otherwise document the question, state your working assumption explicitly, and proceed. Timeout policy (FR-035, amended 2026-09-28): on a downstream MCP transport/request timeout retry ONCE — but only for read-only/idempotent calls; then use the tool's container route when available (the HTTP endpoint reachable from the guidance container, configured per server as containerRoute in downstream-servers.json; agent-side: run_operation through the guidance server) before falling back to local tools; route heavy GitNexus work (analyze/reindex) through the terminal CLI instead of MCP; after a second timeout, or for non-idempotent (workspace_write) calls, escalate via report_blocker (category: infrastructure) instead of retrying.
requiredActions: Run at least one Clear-Thought sequential_thinking or decision_framework pass for decomposition/prioritization and reference the results in the plan submission.

review_and_adjust_plan.title: Review and Adjust the Plan
review_and_adjust_plan.instruction: Review the plan critically from architecture, correctness, maintainability, testability, security, backward-compatibility, performance, and operational perspectives, using the Clear-Thought tools: stress-test the plan's assumptions with assumption_xray, socratic_method, or argument_map, and reference the reasoning results in the findings. Submit the complete adjusted plan. Submission idempotency: never reuse a requestId across submissions — each phase advance requires a fresh requestId; if a submission returns accepted but the phase is unchanged, do not retry the same requestId — check get_workflow_state (requestIds) instead. Ask open questions in the chat before submitting and reference them in `remainingConcerns`; escalate via `report_blocker` ONLY when the answer would materially change this submission (a different plan or different code) — otherwise document the question, state your working assumption explicitly, and proceed. Timeout policy (FR-035, amended 2026-09-28): on a downstream MCP transport/request timeout retry ONCE — but only for read-only/idempotent calls; then use the tool's container route when available (the HTTP endpoint reachable from the guidance container, configured per server as containerRoute in downstream-servers.json; agent-side: run_operation through the guidance server) before falling back to local tools; route heavy GitNexus work (analyze/reindex) through the terminal CLI instead of MCP; after a second timeout, or for non-idempotent (workspace_write) calls, escalate via report_blocker (category: infrastructure) instead of retrying.
requiredActions: Run at least one Clear-Thought stress-test pass (assumption_xray, socratic_method, or argument_map) and reference the results in the findings.

implement.title: Implement the Approved Plan
implement.instruction: Implement the approved plan. Follow the approved task identifiers, avoid unrelated changes, and report all changed, created, and deleted files plus deviations. FIRST step: verify you are in the expected checkout (git status), then ensure a feature branch (feature/<meaningful-name>) exists for this work. LAST step: update the documentation (README.md — documentation is always written in English) and the memory-bank files. Submission idempotency: never reuse a requestId across submissions — each phase advance requires a fresh requestId; if a submission returns accepted but the phase is unchanged, do not retry the same requestId — check get_workflow_state (requestIds) instead. Ask open questions in the chat before submitting and reference them in `unresolvedIssues` (together with `deviations`); escalate via `report_blocker` ONLY when the answer would materially change this submission (a different plan or different code) — otherwise document the question, state your working assumption explicitly, and proceed. Timeout policy (FR-035, amended 2026-09-28): on a downstream MCP transport/request timeout retry ONCE — but only for read-only/idempotent calls; then use the tool's container route when available (the HTTP endpoint reachable from the guidance container, configured per server as containerRoute in downstream-servers.json; agent-side: run_operation through the guidance server) before falling back to local tools; route heavy GitNexus work (analyze/reindex) through the terminal CLI instead of MCP; after a second timeout, or for non-idempotent (workspace_write) calls, escalate via report_blocker (category: infrastructure) instead of retrying.

review_and_fix_implementation.title: Review and Fix the Implementation
review_and_fix_implementation.instruction: Review the implementation for correctness, edge cases, error handling, security, maintainability, duplication, dead code, performance, compatibility, test coverage, and plan conformity. Apply fixes before submitting, using the Clear-Thought tools: run metacognitive_monitoring as a final confidence check before submitting, and debugging_approach for non-trivial findings — reference the results in the findings. For non-trivial scopes (core engine, shared modules, security- or state-machine-relevant changes) the review MUST include an INDEPENDENT reviewer pass (review sub-agent with authorship excluded) over the semantic diff against the governing spec — self-review alone is insufficient. Apply the boundary checklist to every changed code path: (a) boundary values (</==/> on limits, indexes, counts); (b) concurrency, replay and idempotency (same request twice, concurrent callers); (c) optional configuration fields OMITTED by the caller (do not test only the set case); (d) ordering of guard/gate checks relative to exhaustion/termination checks. Submission idempotency: never reuse a requestId across submissions — each phase advance requires a fresh requestId; if a submission returns accepted but the phase is unchanged, do not retry the same requestId — check get_workflow_state (requestIds) instead. Ask open questions in the chat before submitting and reference them in `unresolvedFindings`; escalate via `report_blocker` ONLY when the answer would materially change this submission (a different plan or different code) — otherwise document the question, state your working assumption explicitly, and proceed. Timeout policy (FR-035, amended 2026-09-28): on a downstream MCP transport/request timeout retry ONCE — but only for read-only/idempotent calls; then use the tool's container route when available (the HTTP endpoint reachable from the guidance container, configured per server as containerRoute in downstream-servers.json; agent-side: run_operation through the guidance server) before falling back to local tools; route heavy GitNexus work (analyze/reindex) through the terminal CLI instead of MCP; after a second timeout, or for non-idempotent (workspace_write) calls, escalate via report_blocker (category: infrastructure) instead of retrying.
requiredActions: Run Clear-Thought metacognitive_monitoring as a final confidence check before submitting; when findings are non-trivial, additionally apply debugging_approach and reference the results in the findings.

verify.title: Verify the Implementation
verify.instruction: Guidance will execute the configured verification operations. Analyze failures and return to implementation review when code changes are required. Do not claim success while a mandatory operation is failing. Timeout policy (FR-035, amended 2026-09-28): on a downstream MCP transport/request timeout retry ONCE — but only for read-only/idempotent calls; then use the tool's container route when available (the HTTP endpoint reachable from the guidance container, configured per server as containerRoute in downstream-servers.json; agent-side: run_operation through the guidance server) before falling back to local tools; route heavy GitNexus work (analyze/reindex) through the terminal CLI instead of MCP; after a second timeout, or for non-idempotent (workspace_write) calls, escalate via report_blocker (category: infrastructure) instead of retrying.

complete.title: Complete the Workflow
complete.instruction: Produce the final completion report: summary, changed files, verification results, known limitations, remaining risks, deviations, deferred work, and next steps. MANDATORY FINAL REVIEW — BEFORE producing the report: run an INDEPENDENT final review in a FRESH sub-agent (review tool with authorship excluded, e.g. spawn_agent) over ALL tasks of this session: hand it the complete diff of all commits/changes of this session, the governing spec, and the focus areas cross-task interactions, spec conformance, fail-closed invariants, boundary cases (limits, concurrency/replay/idempotency, omitted optional config), and test coverage adequacy; require an evidence table per finding and an explicit count of open HIGH/CRITICAL findings. Fix every HIGH/CRITICAL finding before completing (with regression coverage); persist every remaining finding in memory-bank/remaining-work-plan.md AND memory-bank/activeContext.md (Findings Lifecycle Rule) and reference the review outcome (scope, findings count, fixes) in the completion report. Completing with open HIGH/CRITICAL findings is not allowed. BEFORE submitting the completion report: refresh the GitNexus index host-side by running gitnexus analyze --no-stats in the repo root (via the configured shell) and note the refresh in the report — the index-freshness gate only verifies index availability, not freshness. Repository analysis endpoint: http://host.docker.internal:4747/api/mcp. (2) review this session for recurring bugs, traps, and validated fixes, and write validated lessons (redacted, [{slug, observation, cause, fix}]) to .guidance/state/session-lessons.json — ALWAYS create the file, using an empty array if there are no validated lessons. The final-review mandate is machine-enforced by the required operation `final-review-gate`: write `.guidance/state/final-review.json` (strict schema, headCommit == HEAD, openHighCritical 0, evidence per finding) AFTER the last commit — any commit after the review invalidates the gate. Ask open questions in the chat before submitting and reference them in `deferredWork`/`nextSteps`; escalate via `report_blocker` ONLY when the answer would materially change this submission (a different plan or different code) — otherwise document the question, state your working assumption explicitly, and proceed. Submission idempotency: never reuse a requestId across submissions — each phase advance requires a fresh requestId; if a submission returns accepted but the phase is unchanged, do not retry the same requestId — check get_workflow_state (requestIds) instead. Before finishing, seed validated lessons via the insight server (http://host.docker.internal:3002/mcp) — the capture-session-lessons gate does this automatically. Timeout policy (FR-035, amended 2026-09-28): on a downstream MCP transport/request timeout retry ONCE — but only for read-only/idempotent calls; then use the tool's container route when available (the HTTP endpoint reachable from the guidance container, configured per server as containerRoute in downstream-servers.json; agent-side: run_operation through the guidance server) before falling back to local tools; route heavy GitNexus work (analyze/reindex) through the terminal CLI instead of MCP; after a second timeout, or for non-idempotent (workspace_write) calls, escalate via report_blocker (category: infrastructure) instead of retrying.
requiredActions: Run an independent final review in a fresh, authorship-excluded sub-agent over ALL tasks of this session (full session diff + governing spec + boundary/concurrency/coverage focus), with an evidence table per finding and an explicit HIGH/CRITICAL count.
Fix every HIGH/CRITICAL finding before completing (with regression coverage); persist all remaining findings in memory-bank/remaining-work-plan.md and memory-bank/activeContext.md.
Reference the final-review outcome (scope, findings count, fixes) in the completion report.
